# Streamlit ### Built in Python. Made for people and agents. Owned by your team. **Streamlit is the agent-native data app framework.** Use it for dashboards, forecasting tools, review-and-approval workflows, and any other app built around your data. [![PyPI downloads](https://img.shields.io/pypi/dm/streamlit?label=PyPI%20downloads)](https://pypi.org/project/streamlit/) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/streamlit/streamlit?style=flat)](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/stargazers) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue)](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/LICENSE) A Streamlit app is just Python, with no separate frontend or API layer. Streamlit is batteries-included and takes care of the hard parts: a consistent, well-designed interface, state, caching, sign-in, theming, and upgrades. Your team keeps only its own logic, written in a language it already reads every day. **The No. 1 Python framework for data apps and dashboards.** [More than a million repositories](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/network/dependents) on GitHub depend on it. Used by millions. Trusted by thousands of companies, from startups to global enterprises. ## What teams build
APPS THAT COMPUTE
Forecasts, simulations, and models with what-if levers
Pricing and demand simulators, risk models, and AI analysis over your data. The computation and the interface are the same Python.
Try the live demo → 		APPS THAT ACT
Review queues, approvals, sign-offs, and writeback
Editable tables (st.data_editor) and forms put the decision in the same app as the data, including approving what an AI agent proposes.
Try the live demo → 		ADVANCED DASHBOARDS
KPI dashboards with drill-down and cross-filtering
Fast over large data. Coming from a BI tool? Move your dashboards to Streamlit, and modernize them on the way.
Try the live demo →
The source for all three is in [streamlit/demos](https://github.com/streamlit/demos). Streamlit is also great for AI and chat apps over your data (`st.chat_input`, `st.write_stream`), ML and model tools, and internal data tools. ## Get started ```bash pip install streamlit ``` ### Build with your coding agent Run [`streamlit skills`](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/cli/skills) in your project folder. It installs our expert skills for Claude Code and any agent that reads the shared `.agents` skills folder, matched to your Streamlit version. So your agent follows current best practices instead of whatever it memorized two versions ago. Then ask, and mention Streamlit so the agent picks up the skills (in Claude Code, `/developing-with-streamlit` works too): > Build a Streamlit app that forecasts demand from `sales.csv`, with what-if levers for > price and growth. ### Or write it yourself Here's a complete app: a demand forecast that planners can adjust and submit for sign-off. Save it as `streamlit_app.py` and run `streamlit run streamlit_app.py`: ```python import sqlite3 import numpy as np import pandas as pd import streamlit as st st.title("Demand plan") @st.cache_data def load_actuals() -> pd.DataFrame: # Swap in your own query, e.g. st.connection("snowflake").query("...") months = pd.date_range("2025-01-01", periods=12, freq="MS") units = 1_000 + 40 * np.arange(12) + np.random.default_rng(0).normal(0, 50, 12) return pd.DataFrame({"month": months, "actual": units.round()}) actuals = load_actuals() growth = st.slider("Monthly growth (%)", -5.0, 10.0, 2.0, step=0.5) months = pd.date_range("2026-01-01", periods=6, freq="MS") baseline = actuals["actual"].iloc[-1] * (1 + growth / 100) ** np.arange(1, 7) forecast = pd.DataFrame({"month": months, "forecast": baseline.round()}) # Planners edit the forecast, and the chart follows plan = st.data_editor(forecast, disabled=["month"], hide_index=True) st.line_chart(pd.concat([actuals, plan]), x="month") if st.button("Submit for sign-off", type="primary"): with sqlite3.connect("plans.db") as db: # Or your warehouse plan.to_sql("plans", db, if_exists="append", index=False) st.success(f"Submitted {len(plan)} months for sign-off.") ``` ## Why Streamlit **Generating an app is cheap. Owning it isn't.** An agent can write a React frontend, a Python backend, and the API between them in an afternoon. Then someone has to review all three, keep them in sync, and patch them for years. With Streamlit, it's one layer of Python, and the plumbing is our job. - **Made for data.** Hand a pandas, Polars, Snowpark, or PySpark dataframe straight to a table or chart. Tables load rows as you scroll, so they stay fast on large data. Native charts cover nearly every visualization, from KPI sparklines to maps and diagrams, and Vega-Lite and ECharts charts switch to faster rendering on their own as the data grows. - **Fast dashboards.** Wrap a section in `@st.fragment`, and only that section reruns when people use it. Cached queries can refresh in the background (`@st.cache_data(ttl=..., refresh_mode="background")`), so nobody waits on a stale query. Chart and table selections (`on_select`) let people cross-filter and drill down, and filters bound to the URL (`bind="query-params"`) make every view shareable. - **Free on the logic. Opinionated on the design.** Write any logic you like, with any Python library. The look comes from Streamlit: native charts, tables, and filters, styled by one [brand theme](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/configuration/theming) that all your apps share. App number 200 looks like it belongs with app number one, no matter who, or what, built it. - **Stable for years.** Breaking changes are extremely rare. Most apps written years ago still run on the latest release, and every upgrade brings them new features, speed, and security fixes. - **Built for agents.** Agents drive the running app without a browser, read the numbers back as data, and leave tests behind for CI ([`AppTest`](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/app-testing)). Turn on the experimental agent API (`server.enableAgentApi`), and Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or any other MCP client can use your app with the same logic and access rules as a person in the browser. There's no second API to build. - **Enterprise-ready.** Built-in sign-in (`st.login`), security scanning on every change with fixes in regular releases, and accessibility built to WCAG 2.2 A and AA, with a [published audit](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/wiki/accessibility-wcag.md). Run it in your own cloud, on [Community Cloud](https://streamlit.io/cloud), or natively [inside Snowflake](https://docs.streamlit.io/deploy/snowflake). - **Escape hatches.** Need a bespoke screen? Drop in a [custom component](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/custom-components/components-v2) written in React or anything else. Need a webhook or your own API route? Add it with [`st.App`](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/server/st.app). ## Community Cloud Deploy, manage, and share your apps for free on [Community Cloud](https://streamlit.io/cloud). Connect a GitHub repository, pick your app file, and your app gets its own `streamlit.app` URL. [Sign up here](https://share.streamlit.io/signup). ## Resources - [Docs](https://docs.streamlit.io) to learn how Streamlit works - [Community forum](https://discuss.streamlit.io) for questions and help - [Blog](https://blog.streamlit.io) for tips from developers and creators - [Components](https://streamlit.io/components) to extend Streamlit ## Contribute Thanks for your interest in helping improve Streamlit! We have paused accepting pull requests from outside the Streamlit maintainer team. You can still make a valuable contribution by [reporting bugs](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml), [requesting features](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/new?template=feature_request.yml), [improving or upvoting existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aopen%20sort%3Areactions-%2B1-desc), [commenting on open specs](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3Achange%3Aspec), creating [custom components](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/custom-components/components-v2), and contributing to [streamlit-extras](https://github.com/arnaudmiribel/streamlit-extras). Read our [contribution guide](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md) for details. ## License Streamlit is completely free and open-source and licensed under the [Apache 2.0](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0) license.
